div.l: Vppon̄ þe see til IħuIhesu Crist him hent
He hadde a crosse of latoıı̄un ful of stones
And in a glasse he had pigges bones
But with thies relikes whan that he fonde
A poer ꝑperson dwelling vpon londe
Vpon a dai he gete him more mony
Than þe ꝑpersoıı̄un gete in monthes twey
And thus with feined flatri and fapes
He made þe ꝑpersoıı̄un and þe peple his apes
But truli to tell atte last
He was in chirche a nobe ecclesiast
Well couth he rede a lesoıı̄un or a storie
But aldest he song an offratorie
For wel he wist whan that was song
He most preche and wel a file his tong
To wyn siluer as he well couthe
Therefore he sang þe meuell and þᵉ loude
Now haue I told you sotheli in a clause
The state the aray þe nūmbre and þe cause
Whi that assembled was this company
In Southwerk at this gentell hostlery
That hight þe Tabard fast bi þe bell
But now is tyme yow for to tell
How that we bere vs þe same night
Whan we were in that ostri a right
And aftr wil I tel of oure viage
And al þe remenaunte of oure pilgrimage
But first I prai yow for youre curtasie
That ye directe not it my vilany
Though I pleinli speke in þis mater
To tel you her wordez and her chere
And thowe I speke her wordez propurly
For this ye knowe aswel as I
Who shal tel a tale aftre a man̄
He most reherse as ny as euer he can
Crist spak him self ful brode in holi writ
And wel he wote no vilany is it
Eke plato seith who can him rede
The worde most be cosin to þe dede
Also I prai you for yif it me
All þogh I haue not set folke in her degre
Her in thies tales as þei shuld stonde
Mi wit is short . ye mai wel vnderstonde
